survey_design: 11 May 2026 is a Monday; the methodology specifies Tue/Wed/Thu and excludes Monday.
May is pre-monsoon peak heat; recommended windows are Oct-Nov or Feb-Mar.
No weekend day surveyed; the stated minimum is three days including Sat and Sun.
U-turns were never counted. Twelve movements per junction, not sixteen.

assumptions.capacity_source: IRC:92-2017 Table 6.3 / Indo-HCM Table 5.4, four-lane divided urban

capacity.lane_model_basis: composition only. The earlier basis - observed flow above saturation flow - held on narrower measured widths and does not hold on the corrected ones, so it is withdrawn rather than restated. If the wide transects turn out to be service roads, the lane counts fall and that basis returns.
capacity.width_caveat: A transect cannot distinguish a through lane from a service road. 43 of 77 transects (56%) measure over 14 m per direction, up to 19.9 m, which is five running lanes each way. That is possible on this corridor and it is also what a service road looks like from above. Capacity scales linearly with this, so treat the wide junctions as an upper bound until the carriageway is confirmed on site.

alternatives.note: The junction already meters the opposing stream. Removing the signal is what creates the gap problem in the first place.

Move it to a chainage where the opposing through flow is lower. Only helps if such a chainage exists within a tolerable detour. It cannot help the 2 bay(s) whose demand is above the 1,800 veh/h a single opening passes at zero opposing traffic, and for the rest the opposing flow would have to fall 91%.

A metered U-turn manufactures the gap the stream will not offer. It reintroduces the signal the scheme exists to remove, on the corridor rather than at the junction. It still cannot serve the 2 bay(s) above the 1,800 veh/h ceiling: metering creates gaps, it does not shorten the follow-up headway.

alternatives.measure: widen the median, add an acceleration lane
alternatives.note: Raises capacity by lowering the follow-up headway and letting vehicles merge rather than cross. A second-order effect on a first-order shortfall. It cannot help the 2 bay(s) whose demand is above the 1,800 veh/h a single opening passes at zero opposing traffic, and for the rest the opposing flow would have to fall 91%.

The only measure that changes the binding term: it removes the conflicting flow rather than asking the U-turn to find gaps in it. For the 2 bay(s) above the ceiling it works by removing the NEED for a U-turn - with the through movement elevated the junction can keep a signalised right turn - not by making the bay work. A single opening still cannot pass their demand.

uturn_framework.measurement_status: provisional: the DWG carries no dimension entities, so every width here is scaled from georeferenced linework and a total station survey is required before design

measurement.source: JDA survey drawing (DWG converted to DXF); no dimension entities present

dimensions.used_for: lane count, approach capacity, v/c, design life, queue length
dimensions.method: perpendicular transects every 5 m, median within 400 m of the junction; total kerb-to-kerb less the median, halved
dimensions.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap interval 0.5 to 6.9 m wide across the six junctions
dimensions.resolved_by: total station cross-sections at each junction and mid-block

dimensions.method: 5 m, chosen where the answer stops moving
dimensions.uncertainty: convergence tested at 25, 10, 5, 2 m; junctions converged: 6 of 6
dimensions.resolved_by: not applicable - this is a property of the method, not the road

dimensions.used_for: junction ordering, U-turn detours, pier siting stations
dimensions.method: cumulative distance along JDA's KML centreline in EPSG:32643
dimensions.uncertainty: the KML carries 14 vertices over 4,625 m, so curvature between vertices is cut off; the polyline is a lower bound on true length
dimensions.resolved_by: a surveyed centreline string, or the CAD alignment once its layer is identified

dimensions.used_for: the assumption that chainage and transects share one geometry
dimensions.method: distance from each centreline station to the nearest CAD linework
dimensions.uncertainty: median 1.36 m to the nearest divider line, 90th percentile 3.92 m
dimensions.resolved_by: a common control point in both, or a stated CAD georeference

dimensions.used_for: whether a U-turn is physically possible at an opening
dimensions.method: gap between consecutive DIVIDER runs, measured along the alignment
dimensions.uncertainty: not quantified per opening - the DIVIDER layer is a single polyline set with no separate edge, so an opening's width has no second reading to compare against
dimensions.resolved_by: total station at each opening: nose to nose, and the receiving carriageway width opposite

dimensions.method: junction chainage to the nearest U-turn-capable opening, doubled
dimensions.uncertainty: carries the chainage uncertainty above, doubled; and 3 of 12 bays lie beyond the drawing so their detour is not measured at all rather than estimated
dimensions.resolved_by: the seven proposed bay chainages from JDA

dimensions.method: perpendicular distance from the alignment to each constraint feature
dimensions.uncertainty: inherits the registration figure above; feature positions are CAD vertices with no stated survey accuracy
dimensions.resolved_by: the drawing's own survey control sheet, if one exists

measurement.status: provisional: every dimension is scaled from georeferenced linework and a total station survey is required before design
